extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, medical educators, museum palaeontologists, entomologists and surveyors)
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards for organising medical education (curriculum, examinations, postgraduate training) and related professional/scientific reporting practices discussed in a Nature magazine issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical manual content and style
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject is treated in a strictly practical way; obsolete methods and historical details find no place; apparatus that every worker must buy is not described with excessive minuteness; theoretical considerations are introduced only when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such information as is necessary for using apparatus to the best advantage; give necessary formulae for operations (making the negative, printing, etching, finishing, mounting, and proofing plates). For complex processes (e.g., three-colour half-tone) assume general knowledge of principles and refer only to additional manipulation necessary. Use numerous useful and good illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial submission and correspondence policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor does not hold himself responsible for opinions expressed by correspondents. He cannot undertake to return, or to correspond with the writers of, rejected manuscripts intended for this or any other part of Nature. No notice is taken of anonymous communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not expect the Editor to engage in correspondence about rejected submissions and should not send anonymous contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for economic entomology species entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Each pest entry gives the technical name, one or two references of interest, a short concise description, notes of the distribution, biology and food plants, and finally the writer's opinion as to the status of the insect as a pest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include figures of adults (and larvae where available). Keep entries brief and systematic so the list serves as an excellent foundation for economic entomologists; a supplementary list may follow as more material becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cave excavation and reporting precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Excavations should be conducted under explicit instructions with precision; deposits should be described stratigraphically with recognition of 'foyers' (surfaces with cinders or products of industry indicating man's presence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear sections of the caves demonstrating positions of foyers and skeletons, include bathymetric charts, avoid assuming objects are in situ without evidence, and record depths (e.g., metres below stalagmite). Precise methods and careful recording render observations beyond dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skelet al description and cautious typology
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe skeletons in detail (stature, skull shape, nose form, orbits, supraciliary eminences, mandible, limb proportions) and compare with other types (Cro-Magnon, Negro, European).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before separating specimens into a distinct type, consider fragmentary preservation, sex, age, and individual variation; avoid overinterpreting stature differences when samples include children or old persons and seek more adult examples before defining new types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of preliminary medical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary and intermediate studies (chemistry, biology, anatomy, physiology) should be concentrated in fewer centres with better equipped laboratories rather than being taught in every medical school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentration would allow some medical schools to devote energies and funds to professional training for the final three years of the curriculum, improving efficiency and reducing expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed multi-centre approach favored over single central institute
rubrics_metrics.description: London is too large for a single central institute; a plan of fewer well-equipped centres (university and a few colleges) is preferable to one central institute requiring large capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical schemes (e.g., drafting hospital students to colleges such as Westminster to King's College) can work satisfactorily and be less costly and more quickly implemented than an ambitious single-centre institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-university science preparation for medical students
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of the chemistry, biology, and physics required for ordinary pass examinations might, and should be, included in public-school science studies and cleared off before the student enters the medical curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pre-university science is covered, the first two years of medical study can be devoted almost entirely to anatomy and physiology (including comparative anatomy and physiological chemistry).

rubrics_metrics.name: State licensing examination for practising medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: With numerous bodies granting qualifications (21 in England, Scotland, Ireland), the practicable way to bring order is the institution of a State examination which everyone should be required to pass irrespective of other degrees or diplomas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standard State exam would reduce variation in standards and conditions of admission among multiple certifying bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: University degree accessibility and role of postgraduate distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The University of London degree should be accessible under reasonable conditions to average students, reserving more stringent honours examinations for those seeking greater distinction; diplomas of Royal Colleges should be more clearly designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the university degree and higher grades as academic distinctions beyond qualification to practise; encourage post-qualification postgraduate work for higher degrees and fellowship/membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of post-graduate study and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-graduation study and research are essential for practitioners to keep abreast of advances and for the advancement of medical science and public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: London's unique clinical material must be better utilized by coordinating and concentrating post-graduate teaching among special hospitals and general hospitals, and by making greater use of poor-law infirmaries and Metropolitan Asylums Board hospitals for clinical and pathological investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital affiliation and consolidation for teaching economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliative grouping or combination of great clinical hospitals about university centres would be of value for financial economy and strength of teaching; many special hospitals are widely scattered and underutilised for teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination of special hospitals and better use of public subscriptions would improve efficiency; the King's Fund supports such views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of hygiene and public health instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching of hygiene and the curriculum for the diploma in public health should be concentrated rather than each medical school retaining expensive equipment for instruction of few students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralised or shared instruction would be more economical and provide better facilities for students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for magnetic survey data collection and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Magnetic surveys must include careful intercomparison of instruments and account for diurnal inequalities and non-cyclic changes; reliance on five 'quiet' days per month may be insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether 'quiet day' inequalities are representative of ordinary days, allow for both regular and irregular diurnal changes when correcting field observations, and be suspicious of large unexplained differences (e.g., between 0 a.m. and 11 p.m.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of bathymetric charts and comprehensive illustrations in geological reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Bathymetric charts and numerous clear illustrations (sections showing positions of features) are deserving of special mention in cave and geological reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include maps/charts and illustrative figures to demonstrate physical relationships and support interpretations; such supporting material strengthens the report's value.
